doom.driver: Ship attack reports near Hormuz reach record high as oil exports slow. BBC Verify analysis of data from a UK maritime agency shows 12 vessels were struck in a week.
doom.blurb: A DOZEN SHIPS STRUCK! THE GULF ABLAZE!
doom.summary: Twelve vessels hit in a single week near Hormuz is no longer a shipping lane; it is a shooting gallery with a toll booth. Ukrainian strikes keep falling on Russian refineries, suspected Russian drones have now hit a tanker inside Romanian waters, and the Oklahoma rancher cursing diesel prices is feeling every one of them. Trump promising no nukes or ground troops in Iran is meant to reassure, which tells you strike options are very much on the table.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Meta's Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter open-weight model, is now free for anyone to download, and AI is reportedly coming for physics after mathematics.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: The FTC is probing Anthropic and OpenAI even as the president calls AI fears a hoax, and Russia is back at the G20 table over European objections.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Record ship attacks near Hormuz, Russian drones inside NATO territorial waters and Houthi missiles hitting Yemen's presidential palace add up to several active fronts at once.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Wired reports that AI-enabled hacks are causing damage nobody is paying for, while zero-click spyware is now being delivered through ordinary targeted ads.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: US-imposed Starlink speed limits are disrupting Ukrainian battlefield missions, which shows how one company's settings can tilt a war.

doom.dalle_prompt:
Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Night scene at the small dhow harbor of Khasab on the Musandam Peninsula, Oman. Black limestone cliffs rise straight out of the town and fill the upper frame as a jagged silhouette, and their lower faces glow dull blood orange from sodium quay lamps. The camera sits low on the concrete quay and looks out across flat, oily black water toward the Strait of Hormuz. Far off on the dark horizon, a long, motionless row of tanker deck lights sits at anchor, all stuck in place, with a faint ember-orange smear low on the sky. Cool tones are nearly extinguished, and the only light is volcanic orange underlighting against deep black.

In the foreground, a storm-battered shipping container from a sunk feeder ship lies half-dragged onto the quay. It is rust-red with peeling paint, its doors hanging open, and spilled cargo and crushed cardboard spread around it. A salvage worker in a hi-vis vest and hard hat pushes a wide broom through the debris, throwing a long stretched shadow across the wet concrete. Beside him, a harbor tug idles at the quay edge with its orange work floodlights burning. Beyond it, a curved floating oil boom encloses a drifting slick of bobbing blue-grey and orange containers and plastic crates, lit from below like embers.

Several wooden dhows with high bows are moored along the quay, their ropes coiled and their hulls scorched orange on one side by the lamplight. A single fisherman sits on an upturned crate mending a net, his back to the strait. Deep shadows dominate, with hard pixel-dithered gradients and a quiet, exhausted, waiting mood.

dawn.summary: A tiny retinal implant called Prima is giving vision back to people with age-related macular degeneration, a condition that affects more than five million people and that no treatment had ever reversed. Now approved in Europe, it turns a once-final diagnosis into something with a path forward. Medicine had more to offer today too: USC researchers found a way to grow a potentially endless supply of cancer-fighting immune cells, and a breast-milk-sugar probiotic sharply cut respiratory infections in formula-fed babies.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Scientists traced how exercise reverses muscle aging to a single gene, DEAF1, opening a clear target for keeping bodies strong for longer.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Qatar announced a massive solar plant project in Lebanon, a major investment in clean power for Lebanese homes.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: The Milwaukee Brewers rallied for a 6-4 comeback to sweep the NLCS and reach their first World Series since 1982.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Researchers identified a 'Pac-Man' enzyme that helps bacteria devour certain plastics, a promising new tool for cleaning up plastic waste.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A Rhode Island farmer grew a 3,156-pound pumpkin, beating a world record that had stood for barely a week.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. GROUND-LEVEL VIEW looking steeply upward from the paving stones of a small town park in clear midday daylight. A huge canopy of fresh spring-green maple leaves fills the upper frame, with shafts of clear golden-yellow light breaking through patches of pale sky. Dappled gold and green light falls evenly across the path, and the mood is steady and confident. In the middle distance, seen from below, an elderly woman sits upright on a wooden park bench. Her cardigan is mustard yellow and her silver hair is lit gold at the edges. She holds an open paperback high at chest level, and its pages are rows of tiny dark dashes. She wears slim glasses with a tiny camera lens on the bridge, and a thin cable runs from the temple down to a palm-sized handheld processor with three small buttons, resting under her thumb in her lap. A small, bright glint of golden light sits at the exact center of the page, where her gaze lands. Her chin is lowered and her mouth is parted in quiet wonder. At the bottom edge of the frame, a child's sneakers and a small hand rest on the bench slats beside her, and a folded crossword with half the squares filled sticks out of a canvas tote at her feet. A few green leaves drift down through the foreground. The bench legs and her shoes loom large at the bottom of the frame, and the canopy narrows toward the top. The palette is golden-yellow, fresh leaf green, cream, and warm tan, with only a touch of teal on the camera glasses and processor.
